passages.title: Brave Now
passages.body: When I was little, I used to be afraid of almost everything. I was afraid of the dark, afraid of dogs, and even afraid of speaking in front of the class. My hands would shake and my face would turn red. My mother always told me, "Everyone feels scared sometimes. Being brave does not mean you have no fear. It means you keep going even when you are afraid." Her words stayed in my mind. Little by little, I tried to face my fears. I started by reading a poem aloud at home, then in front of my family, and finally in class. Last week, I gave a speech to the whole school. I was still a little nervous, but I did it. I am not the shy child I used to be.

passages.title: A Class Reunion
passages.body:
Anna: Is that you, Ben? You look so different! You used to be really short, didn't you?
Ben: Haha, yes! And I used to be very quiet too. I never said a word in class.
Anna: I remember! Now you're tall and you talk to everyone. What changed?
Ben: I joined the school basketball team. It made me taller and gave me confidence. What about you? You used to have long hair.
Anna: I cut it last year. And I didn't use to like reading, but now I read a book every week.
Ben: People really change in a few years, don't they?
Anna: They do. It's nice to see how far we've both come.

passages.title: Why People Change
passages.body: Why do people change as they grow up? Scientists say there are many reasons. First, our bodies change. A child who used to be the shortest in class may become the tallest as a teenager. Second, our interests change. Many people who used to hate vegetables enjoy them as adults. Third, our experiences shape us. A student who used to be afraid of speaking may become confident after joining a club or winning a competition. Change is a normal part of life. It does not happen overnight; it happens slowly, day by day. The important thing is not to compare yourself with others, but to notice how far you have come from the person you used to be.

passages.title: A Letter to My Younger Self
passages.body: Dear younger me, I know you are scared right now. You are afraid of the dark, afraid of making mistakes, and afraid that others will laugh at you. I want you to know that things will get better. You used to think you were not good enough, but you are wrong. In a few years, you will stand on a stage and sing in front of hundreds of people. You won't believe it now, but it is true. The shy, quiet child you are today will grow into someone brave and kind. So please, don't give up. Take small steps every day. Be patient with yourself. The fears that feel so big now will one day feel very small. With love, your future self.

passages.title: Is Change Always Good?
passages.body: Most people agree that change can be a good thing. A shy child who becomes confident, or a lazy student who learns to work hard — these are changes we admire. However, not all change is good. Some people who used to be kind become selfish when they get rich or famous. Some who used to love reading stop because they spend all their time on their phones. So change itself is not always good or bad; what matters is the direction. We should welcome changes that make us better people, and be careful about changes that take us away from who we want to be. The goal is not just to change, but to grow.

passages.title: Youth Club Notice: 'The New Me' Sharing Day
passages.body: GREENWOOD YOUTH CLUB invites you to our 'The New Me' Sharing Day! Have you changed a lot in the past few years? Come and share your story! WHEN: Saturday, May 18th, 2:00 p.m. - 4:00 p.m. WHERE: Club Hall, 2nd floor. WHAT TO DO: Tell us in three minutes how you used to be and how you have changed. You can bring old photos! PRIZES: The three most inspiring stories will win a free book of their choice. SIGN UP: Write your name on the list outside Room 201 before May 15th. Everyone is welcome — whether you used to be shy, afraid, or just very different. We believe every story can inspire someone else!
